title: fix(rest): cross-object POST /batch requires a real transaction and answers 501 on a runtime that cannot roll back
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D6onSP3rxhKmH6GBf9squ19)_

Fixes #32604

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：跨对象批量接口 `POST /batch` 现在向引擎要求「真事务」；在不能回滚的数据库驱动上（托管环境用的远程 Turso），它直接答 `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED`，一条都不写，而不是一条条写下去。
- 为什么改：这个接口对外承诺「要么全成、要么全不成」，但在不能回滚的驱动上，引擎会退化成无事务执行：第二步失败时，第一步写进去的数据留在库里，客户端却以为整批已回滚。在 main 上实测复现：第二步报 404，第一步的那行数据仍在库中。
- 风险与回滚：只改 `packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts` 一处调用和它的错误映射；能回滚的驱动（SQL、内存、MongoDB 等）行为完全不变。受影响的只有本来就不能保证原子性的运行时，那里批量接口从「悄悄写一半」变为「明确拒绝」；发现文档 `capabilities.transactionalBatch` 在这类运行时早已答 `false`，控制台本就不会提供原子批量。没有新的错误码或规格字段。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts`（`ql.transaction(runOps, context, { require: true })` 与其 catch 中的 501 映射）、`packages/rest/src/rest-batch-no-rollback-driver.test.ts`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest exec vitest run src/rest-batch-no-rollback-driver.test.ts`，预期 6 passed。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

One package, `@objectstack/rest`, one route. No new export, error code, spec key or wire field.

- **`batch-routes.ts`, cross-object `POST /batch`.** The transaction callback is now a named `runOps`, and the route calls `ql.transaction(runOps, context, { require: true })` (#5696). On a default driver that fails `driverSupportsTransactions` (no `beginTransaction`, or one inherited and denied by `supports.transactionsUnsupported`, as `TursoDriver` declares on its remote transport), the engine throws `TransactionUnsupportedError` (`ERR_TRANSACTION_UNSUPPORTED`) before the callback runs, instead of taking the ADR-0119 D1 degrade. The route maps that refusal to the same `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` body it already answers for an engine without `transaction()`. The mapping is limited to the engine's up-front refusal: an `entered` flag set as the callback starts keeps any error from inside the ops on its existing path (`handleRouteError`).
- **The refusal predicate** (`isTransactionUnsupportedRefusal`) compares the registered code string: `@objectstack/objectql`, which exports `TRANSACTION_UNSUPPORTED_CODE`, is only a dev dependency of this package, and the error's own header prescribes judging by `code` across package boundaries.
- **Discovery is unchanged.** `capabilities.transactionalBatch` is already produced by `getDiscovery()` from `engineCanRollBack(engine)` (#18997), which reads the same default driver through the same `driverSupportsTransactions`, and the REST layer ANDs it with `api.enableBatch`. The new test pins it end to end on both runtimes.

## Why

#32604: the route documents itself "all-or-nothing by construction" but only checked `typeof ql.transaction`. On a runtime that cannot roll back, a batch whose later op failed kept its earlier ops' rows, and the client was told nothing. Triage 6837448745 set the direction (declared ≠ enforced, made loud); real transactions on remote Turso stay with #32500 / #32481.

## Acceptance notes

- **Step 0 on `main` 5fb79bc0** (same test file, real `ObjectQL` + `SqlDriver` subclass declaring `transactionsUnsupported` + real protocol + real route): the failing batch answered `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` with the `nrb_alpha` row `a-1` left in the table; the all-good batch answered `200` with both rows written. The rollback-capable controls were already green.
- **Discovery parity, one residual population.** Where no default driver resolves (none registered, or the default unregistered), `engineCanRollBack` answers `true` while the engine's `require: true` refuses, so discovery advertises the batch and the route answers 501. That is the refusal side (nothing is written) and is pre-existing in the predicate; not changed here.
- **Other populations that now get 501 instead of a degraded write:** any runtime whose default driver lacks `beginTransaction` or declares `transactionsUnsupported` (remote Turso; an OData default). Discovery already answered `false` on each.
- **Out of scope, noted:** the per-object atomic batch (`runAtomicBatch` in `protocol-batch-data.ts`) still calls `engine.transaction(cb)` without `require: true`; it gates on `engineCanRollBack` first, so it differs only in the no-default-driver population above. Writes to ledger objects on a non-default datasource run outside the transaction by declared design (`engine-execute-transactions.ts`). Neither is a defect this card owns.
- Independent red-line re-read (xhigh): no partial write survives on a no-rollback runtime (the refusal precedes the callback; the ambient-join branch is unreachable there because only a real `beginTransaction` publishes an ambient unit); nothing changes on a driver that can roll back (`require` is read only inside the engine's non-transactional branch; the rethrow keeps error identity).

## Tests

`packages/rest/src/rest-batch-no-rollback-driver.test.ts` (new), real engine, protocol and route:

- No-rollback driver: a 2-op cross-object batch whose second op fails answers `501` with the route's `{ error, code: 'NOT_IMPLEMENTED' }` body and leaves both tables empty; an all-good batch also answers `501` with nothing written (the refusal precedes any write); discovery says `transactionalBatch.enabled: false`.
- Controls on `SqlDriver`: the failing batch keeps `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` with nothing persisted; the good batch commits with `200` and both rows; discovery says `true`.

## Verification

All readings on head `b8dcd99c30` (branch tip; `origin/main` was still `5fb79bc0` when merged, so the merge was a no-op).

The no-rollback failing batch answered `404 {"error":"Record no-such-row not found in nrb_beta","code":"RECORD_NOT_FOUND"}` with `nrb_alpha` holding row `a-1`; the good batch answered `200` with both rows.
- On the head: the same file 6/6 passed, beside `rest-batch-endpoint`, `rest-batch-blank-id`, `batch-op-exposure-object-read`, `rest-batch-size-cap` and `objectql-slot-consumer-census` (6 files, 81 tests passed).

Fixed by keeping the sentence there; that file is green on the head.
